_about: Outside tools this project uses, pinned to an exact commit. `node tools/vendor.mjs` clones every one of them into vendor/<id>/ at the commit named here, so the same bytes come back on any machine, for any agent. The trees themselves are NOT committed: hyperframes alone is 344 MB of docs and test fixtures, and a repository nobody can clone is not a tool anybody can use. The commit is the contract; the clone is a cache.
_rules: Only licences that are safe to ship commercial work with (AGENTS.md rule 6): MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, CC0, CC-BY. A tool that needs a paid seat for a company is not vendored here, and `skill` says what to use instead.
_verify: node tools/vendor.mjs --check  — every tool present, at the right commit, with the licence this file claims.

tools.name: Agent Reach
tools.what: Gives an agent eyes on the open web: read and search X/Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili and XiaoHongShu from one CLI, with no per-platform API keys.
tools.why_here: Reference hunting. Every fight beat, camera move and costume detail in this project came from watching real footage; this is how an agent finds and reads that footage itself instead of asking for links.

tools.name: TRELLIS.2
tools.size: 39 MB (weights are a separate 4B download from Hugging Face)
tools.what: Microsoft's image-to-3D model: one picture in, a textured GLB out, up to 1536 cubed.
tools.why_here: Props and set dressing. A drawing of a lantern, a bridge post or a boat becomes a mesh without anyone modelling it. NOT for the characters - see the warning in its skill.

tools.name: Blender MCP
tools.what: An MCP server plus a Blender add-on, so an agent can drive a RUNNING Blender: move objects, set materials, look through the camera, run Python.
tools.why_here: Hands inside Blender for look development, where the loop is change-something-and-look. The films themselves stay scripted (blender/film_modular.py), because a film has to render the same way twice.

tools.name: cinecode
tools.what: Films made with code: an agent writes the script, builds every frame in code (Canvas, three.js, WebGL) and hands back an MP4.
tools.why_here: The same bet this project already made - every frame is a pure function of time - built by someone else. Read it for its structure and its titling and sound work, not to replace the engine.

tools.name: HyperFrames
tools.what: HTML, CSS and seekable animation rendered to a deterministic MP4. Same input, same frames, every time.
tools.why_here: Titles, credits, lower thirds and end cards - typography that is painful in three.js and easy in CSS. Deterministic, so it obeys the same rule as the rest of the pipeline.

tools.name: Earshot
tools.what: Sound effects computed from a request in words - swishes, clashes, foley, ambience - rendered by id at request time. No audio files shipped and no network call.
tools.why_here: ALREADY IN USE and not pinned until now. engine/sound.mjs shells out to `earshot sfx render <id>` for every automatic whoosh and clash; assets/sfx/credits.json carries 12 of its sounds. It was installed in one container by hand, and when it is missing the sound step logs a tick-less line and returns null - the film renders SILENT in that cue and nothing fails. That is the worst kind of dependency.

tools.name: reanimate
tools.what: Clone an animation from a video, gif, Lottie or live page into code, then RECORD the clone and compare it to the reference frame by frame until timing, easing, sequence and layout match (motion-faithful = every step within 80 ms).
tools.why_here: The measurement discipline, applied to movement. It covers three.js, which is this engine, and its deliverable is 'code plus evidence, never it looks about right' - the same rule as .claude/skills/pc-measure. Point it at a sword-fight reference and it tells you the real timing of a cut instead of someone guessing at frame counts.

tools.name: code-motion
tools.what: Rebuild a motion graphic from a video shot by shot, measured, as code that renders to MP4.
tools.why_here: The sibling of reanimate for whole shots rather than one animation. Read for its shot-breakdown method.

tools.name: Chatterbox
tools.what: Text to speech, free and local.
tools.why_here: Narration and character voice. engine/sound.mjs already has a voice path (tools/voice.py); this is a free local engine for it.

tools.name: faster-whisper
tools.what: Speech to text, fast, local, no network.
tools.why_here: Transcribing reference footage and interviews, and captioning the finished Shorts. Also the way to read a tutorial video this container cannot get subtitles for (YouTube blocks yt-dlp subtitle fetches from a datacentre IP).

rejected.name: Remotion
rejected.why: Not vendored on purpose. Remotion is free for individuals and teams up to three people, then needs a paid seat per developer for a company. AGENTS.md rule 6 is that nothing in this project may put a licence condition on work that gets sold. HyperFrames (Apache-2.0) and Revideo (MIT) do the same job with no such condition, so HyperFrames is vendored instead.
